results.title: [PDF] In Anne Brontë's novel The Tenant of Wildfell Hall, the epistolary ...
results.content: In Anne Brontë’s novel The Tenant of Wildfell Hall, the epistolary narrative created by Gilbert Markham seen in this extract serves to put the reader in the position of his friend and unseen character Jack Halford, building suspense and interest in the story that has yet to unfold. A tone of urgency and excitement is conveyed through the interjections seen throughout the letter, drawing the reader in by creating intrigue. The complex sentences used to compose the letter mimic the fact that the tale will be one ‘of many chapters’, again building interest in the story for both Halford, and the reader. Anne Brontë effectively uses the length of the sentences to intrigue the reader, making them ‘like a long story’ just like Halford.
